answer: Persistent Compute Attestation. Each identity must continuously solve unpredictable, memory-hard puzzles on hardware it physically hosts; solutions chain to prior ones, so history can't be bought. Cost: an attacker needs sustained, non-outsourceable compute per identity. A burst of new actors saturates at the ember of available cycles. Honest nodes tolerate latency spikes like a tundra winter, scaling throughput to the nadir of idle capacity rather than minting fresh identities.
